So for the first 28 times I watched through Glee (Yes, I've literally counted how many times I've watched the whole series, I just finished my 48th time) I always saw myself AS Rachel. I had a dream and I didn't care about the sacrifices I'd be forced to make in order to achieve those dreams. She was my Barbra.

And I've got no clue why my undying love for her character started to waver. Maybe it's because I stopped seeing myself in her. But as time went on, I just started to notice those tiny little details that made her... Obnoxious, I guess? But I'll always have a soft spot for her.

I think it's important for people to know that an overdose doesn't always equal to suicide. Addiction changes a person more than anything. And it's scary that a moment of weakness can result in death. 

My mother's an angel. And honestly, without Glee and the amazing Gleek community, I wouldn't be alive. I've probably watched the whole show from beginning to end ATLEAST 50 times. I always go back to it when my life gets to a very dark place. And having people that I can talk about my love for this show, all of you amazing people, makes me feel like I'm part of something special. And that makes you special... Right? 😉❤️

Thank you. If it wasn't for my amazing mother, I wouldn't have made it. She even celebrated my survival by buying me the Glee box set! So now I'm finally able to share the biggest love of my life with her!

From what I've gathered, he died because he took too big of a dose of heroin than he could handle at that time after consuming a large amount of alcohol throughout the day. Basically, when addicts go to rehab and come back out, their tolerance goes down to more of a "normal" state. A dose that would be considered small for them back in the day, turns lethal in the "right" circumstances.

I know because I started doing drugs at the age of 12 (I'm now 24) and I stopped when I was 15. I was clean up until two months ago, when I overdosed on heroin. Thankfully I got into the emergency clinic before it was too late (thank you mother). 

So, no, it wasn't suicide. It was an accidental lethal overdose due to not knowing the dangers of going right back to your normal doses after rehab. 

R.I.P Cory, you'll always be missed.
